title: Verify Preorder Serialization of a Binary Tree
prompt:
One way to serialize a binary tree is to use pre-order traversal. When encountering a non-null node, record that node's value as a string. If it's a null node, record `"#"` instead. Given a comma-separated string `preorder` representing such a serialization, determine whether it is a valid pre-order serialization of some binary tree, without reconstructing the tree.

Each value in the string is either an integer or the character `'#'`, separated by commas.

examples.explanation: This is a valid pre-order serialization of a binary tree with 9 as root, 3 and 2 as its children, and so on.
A single node needs two null markers (for its two children) to be complete; this string only has one.
A lone '#' represents an entirely empty tree, which is a valid (if minimal) pre-order serialization.

constraints: preorder consists of integers in the range [0, 100] and '#' separated by commas ','
hints: Think of every non-null node as consuming one 'available slot' (it needs a parent slot to occupy) while opening up two new slots (for its own two children); a '#' consumes one slot and opens none.

Track a running count of available slots, starting at 1 (for the root). Each token processed must have at least one slot available to consume; if the count ever hits zero before the string ends, the serialization is invalid.

A valid serialization uses up every slot exactly by the end: after processing all tokens, the slot count must be exactly 0, and it must never go negative or hit zero early with tokens still remaining.

solution.approach: Model the string as consuming and producing 'slots': initially there is 1 slot available (for the root). Every token (number or '#') consumes one slot. A number additionally produces two new slots (for its left and right children); a '#' produces none. Process tokens left to right, decrementing the slot count for each token and adding 2 more slots after a number token. If the slot count ever drops to 0 or below while tokens remain (a slot was consumed but the tree closed off too early, or was over-consumed), the serialization is invalid. It's valid if and only if the slot count is exactly 0 after processing every token.
